anti_generic_signature_read: Asked cold what it would still remember a week later that a generic version would not give it: 'The size ladder itself -- that the pieces are not uniform tokens but eight different-sized worlds on identical feet, so the board has a built-in hierarchy you can read at a glance from across the table.' It reached that before it knew a fifth root of real planetary diameter was involved. Also 'the spiky cyan cones planted on a black square, which look like ice needles growing out of the board', and 'the deep blue globe's grey spot with a tiny satellite dot stuck to its edge'.
blind_action_read: 'Image 1 invites placing and moving pieces from square to square on a grid, two sides distinguished by white feet versus black feet... The two dimpled trays invite parking or storing eight pieces each, one tray per side, since the scoops match the plinth diameter... The cones and textured tiles sit in the path across the board, so they invite being treated as obstacles or special squares to route around.'
blind_form_read: 'The pieces themselves are a stack of three volumes: a wide shallow cylinder foot, a short narrow cylinder collar, and a sphere.' Of the board: 'a thick flat plate, low and rectangular, with a plain flat border rim and an inset playing field of square tiles... Everything on the board is round and everything under it is flat.' It found the terrain unprompted: 'a large block of brown-orange tiles carrying rows of small raised pyramids', 'a peach-tan patch at the lower left with etched starburst lines', 'a black square at the upper right flanked by cyan tiles', and 'slender pointed cones' standing proud of them.
blind_held_read: Unprompted, before anything was revealed: 'a small standing playing piece: a ball on a round plinth, like a chess pawn whose head is a planet... the foot's vertical rim carries a small stamped character', and of the set: 'a tabletop grid game with planet pieces, a board, and two piece-holding trays'.
blind_relationship_read: 'Each sphere sits on its collar on its plinth, and the plinth sits on a tile.' 'Sizes are causally ordered: every piece sits on an identically sized plinth, so only the ball changes, and the ball diameters step down in a consistent ladder.' 'The black square sits inside the cyan etched tiles at the upper right, and the peach etched tiles at the lower left mirror that arrangement diagonally across the board.'
blind_subjects_read: 'Planets.' All eight named cold from the ladder frames, each with the cue recorded at the time: 'a fat orange-and-cream banded globe with a small dark red oval spot low on its left; a pale yellow globe with a ring; a plain cyan globe with a thin pale ring seen almost edge-on around its rim; a deep blue globe with white bands and a grey spot; a small globe with green landmasses on blue sea and white at the top; a pale cream globe with a single wavy lighter band; a red globe with orange-white blotches; and a small grey globe with one bright ring-shaped crater and one brown patch.'

critical_form_requirements.blind_evidence: Found unprimed in round 1 on both globes independently, before the critic knew an edition existed: image 5, 'A small grey circle, about a quarter the width of the oval, touching the oval's lower-left edge'; image 6, 'A small grey circle, about a quarter the oval's width, touching the oval's lower edge'. Asked whether the two pieces carry the same marks it answered 'Yes... both carry three bands... one grey oval, and one small grey circle'.
critical_form_requirements.requirement: On BOTH Neptune pieces there is a small marking just south of the Great Dark Spot that was not there before.

critical_form_requirements.blind_evidence: Round 1 named exactly one on each globe, singular, in an exhaustive five-item enumeration of every mark it could see per piece. Round 2, re-checking: 'there is exactly one added mark per globe, no stray dots, no doubled copy.'
critical_form_requirements.requirement: It is ONE mark, not several.

critical_form_requirements.blind_evidence: This is the one requirement the repair had to earn. Round 1, unprimed, called it 'a small grey circle' on both pieces. Round 2, after the keep-out separated it from the spot: 'It now reads as an oval on the Sol piece and as a rounded oval on the Anti piece', measured by the critic at 40x24 px and 38x28 px in projection. The critic disclosed this observation as primed. The oval is 10 by 5 degrees of great-circle arc by construction; measure/neptune-atlas-resolution.md walks the built ring.
critical_form_requirements.requirement: It is an oval wider than it is tall, not a round dot.

critical_form_requirements.blind_evidence: Round 1 reported the offsets as a discrepancy -- 'attached at the oval's lower-left in image 5 and at the oval's lower-centre-right in image 6'. Round 2 withdrew that as its own error once told the two armies lean opposite ways: 'the offsets are mirrored -- down-and-left on Sol, down-and-right on Anti, with the vertical component nearly identical on both (about 35 and 39 px) and the horizontal component reversed in sign. That is exactly what a true-south offset looks like on two globes leaning opposite ways by the same axial tilt.'
critical_form_requirements.requirement: It sits on the Great Dark Spot's own meridian, directly south of it rather than off to one side.

critical_form_requirements.blind_evidence: The blocking finding of round 1 and the reason for the repair: unprimed, the critic called the pair 'a notched figure-eight' and 'one two-lobed object'. Round 2 on the repaired build: 'Separate. This is the question my blocking finding turned on, and it is resolved... I can no longer produce the round-one read of "one two-lobed object" even trying to.' It verified by machine as well as by eye: 'the new mark is its own connected region on both globes, and of the 132 pixels immediately surrounding it on the Sol piece and 136 on the Anti piece, zero are marking -- every neighbour is blue.'
critical_form_requirements.requirement: It reads as a SEPARATE mark of its own rather than as part of the Great Dark Spot.

critical_form_requirements.blind_evidence: Round 2, R1: 'Yes, on both pieces... a clean blue channel, a crescent lane of roughly even width, curving round the new mark's inboard side... they run parallel with blue between them all the way.' Its own pixel measurement of closest approach, 9.0 px on Sol and 9.2 px on Anti at 900x900, matches the designed uniform keep-out. measure/neptune-atlas-resolution.md measures it on the rings at 0.4203 mm, 1.05 nozzle widths.
critical_form_requirements.requirement: There is a printable strip of bare globe between the new mark and the dark spot, all the way round it.

critical_form_requirements.blind_evidence: Not a thing an image can settle, and the critic said so; it is measured in measure/neptune-atlas-resolution.md, which walks the built ring and returns 0.886 mm, 2.21 nozzle widths at 0.40 mm, against this set's own floor of one nozzle width (the 0.40 mm strip of green on Earth's outback boundary). What the critic did settle blind is that the mark survives as a distinct feature all the way down to set-photograph scale: round 2, 'On the Anti ladder, Neptune's dark spot sits near the left limb and the companion is visible below it as a tiny but distinctly separate dot with blue between.'
critical_form_requirements.requirement: The new mark's narrowest white is at or above the narrowest-feature limit this set already uses for printable markings.

critical_form_requirements.blind_evidence: Round 1 enumerated all three on each globe unprimed -- two bright ones close-paired in the upper half and one duller one low down, mirrored between the armies -- and round 2 confirmed 'none is broken, interrupted, or clipped by the new mark or by the dark oval'. The critic flagged honestly that closure round the far side cannot be settled from frames that each show one hemisphere.
critical_form_requirements.requirement: Neptune's three white cloud bands are still there, unbroken, at the same latitudes and the same unequal widths.

critical_form_requirements.blind_evidence: Round 2, asked to be blunt: 'At native viewing size, in both images 5 and 6, the dark oval reads as one oval with a bite taken out of its southern rim... Does it read as damage? Not at any scale a person will actually meet it. On the printed piece the oval is 28 degrees across -- about 5.3 mm -- and the bay is 3.7 degrees deep, about 0.7 mm. At that size it reads as two cloud features nested against each other, which is what it is.' It also named the cost exactly: magnified five times it tips toward a comma on the Sol piece and a crescent on the Anti piece. That is recorded in the product's limitations in those words.
critical_form_requirements.requirement: The Great Dark Spot is still one oval in the same place, and the bay the new mark's keep-out cuts in its southern rim does not read as damage.

critical_form_requirements.blind_evidence: Round 1, unprimed, enumerated all eight worlds and their markings one line each and reported 'no other piece carries a small grey satellite blob of the kind added to Neptune, and nothing else in the set looks newly appended'. Round 2 re-checked the whole-set frame, the state sheet and both rank ladders: 'No... they are as they were: sixteen pieces in the same positions in the iso frame, the same three terrain patches, the same cone placements... and both ladders in the same order with the same eight worlds.' The critic was right to say an eye cannot certify this; measure/occurrence-geometry.md does, occurrence by occurrence against the published assembly.
critical_form_requirements.requirement: No other piece in the set carries a new, missing or altered marking.

critical_form_requirements.blind_evidence: Reached cold in round 1 as the single most memorable thing about the object, quoted above, before the critic knew the sizes encoded anything. Round 2, Q1: 'Yes. The size ladder is the thing, and it works... That is the product succeeding at its core claim on a stranger who had no idea what he was looking at... I would want it on a table.'
critical_form_requirements.requirement: The set still reads as one desirable object whose signature claim -- rank you can see -- arrives unaided.

largest_risk: The critic's own words, sealed unedited, from round 1 and unchanged by the repair: 'Legibility of the fine markings at the size they are actually printed and actually viewed. The set sells astronomical detail, but its finest features sit at the resolution floor, and this edition is the proof case: a 1.91 x 0.96 mm feature against a 0.40 mm nozzle is two to five nozzle widths, so shape and tone both degrade... Everything distinctive about the edition lives below the threshold at which a player at the table can see it.' Its round-2 recommendation is recorded with it: ship, but check a physical sample under ordinary room lighting before the render-based tone question is called closed. Nothing in this run has been printed, so that check has not happened.
resolution: TWO ROUNDS, ONE REPAIR, ONE CRITIC. Round 1, unprimed, returned one blocking defect: the spot was cut back to the companion's own outline, the two colours shared a boundary, and a reader with no brief saw 'a notched figure-eight' and called the new marking 'a small grey circle' budding off the spot -- the figure the Wish asked for, inverted. THE GEOMETRY WAS CHANGED, NOT THE PROSE: the spot is now cut to a never-drawn keep-out, the companion's oval grown by 2.30 deg of arc, leaving a measured 0.4203 mm (1.05 nozzle widths) of bare globe between the companion and where the dark stops. All six images were re-rendered; round 2 read the new ones, disclosed as primed, and returned 'No blocking visual defect remains in this build.' THE COST IS NAMED: the spot's body falls from the archive's 11.9319 mm3 to 10.5113, a bay 15.3 deg wide and 3.7 deep in its southern rim; measure/neptune-mirror.md measures its own region BEFORE the cut at the archive's exact 11.9319 and accounts every cubic millimetre of the difference to the keep-out. THE SECOND FINDING WAS MEASURED, NOT REPAIRED: the critic also called the mark grey. measure/neptune-tone-separation.md renders the piece twice at one camera with only that region's filament changed -- 34.5 luma levels from the spot's filament on Sol and 52.5 on Anti-Sol, against this set's shipped floor of 9.4 (Saturn) and 20.2 (Venus). The dim reading is the renderer lighting a southern marking from above, corroborated by the critic's own unprimed round-1 note that the same globe's southernmost white band was 'the darkest of the three bands'. It withdrew the blocking call and asked for the PICTURE to change, and for a printed sample under room light; both asks are in the product's limitations, unmet. print_gate_sha256s is empty and the product is sealed digitally-verified-not-print-ready: no print-readiness is claimed.
reviewer: One independent critic, two rounds, given only this build's canonical renders. Round 1 was unprimed and found a blocking defect; it was repaired and round 2 is the same critic, primed.
